elaine: Heads-up — ran into confusing behavior in the sample app error surface. The JS SDK unwraps 429 into a RetryableError class, but the Python sample app just treats it as a plain HTTPError with a 429 code. New users keep copy/pasting the sample and are surprised by no `should_retry` helper.

raj: Ugh, yeah that mismatch bites. Is the root cause missing typed exceptions in python SDK or sample app omission?

elaine: Looks like both. SDK has typed classes in v2 but the sample app on the docs site still uses the generic requests wrapper. Example from the sample README:

```
try:
  resp = client.generate(...)
except Exception as e:
  print('call failed', e)
```

No retry hints, no Retry-After handling.

sam: On the service side we do send `Retry-After` for rate limits and 503s for capacity. If SDKs surfaced a standard exception shape (RetryableError with .retry_after) it would make sample apps straightforward.

raj: Agreed. Proposal: unify across SDKs with these primitives: `RedwoodError` base, `ClientError` (4xx non-retryable except 429), `RetryableError` (429, 503), `AuthError` (401/403), and include `.status_code`, `.retry_after` (optional), `.raw_body`. Also attach a stable error_code string (e.g., `rate_limit`, `insufficient_capacity`, `invalid_api_key`).

elaine: Love the stable error_code idea — helps docs and mapping tables. For onboarding/playground samples we should provide a tiny helper: `should_retry(err) -> enum {NO, BACKOFF, FAST_RETRY}` and a one-line snippet people can paste.

raj: I'll sketch the Python interface today. Rough draft: 

```
class RedwoodError(Exception): pass
class RetryableError(RedwoodError):
    def __init__(self, status_code, retry_after=None, error_code=None, raw=None):
        self.status_code = status_code
        self.retry_after = retry_after
        self.error_code = error_code
        self.raw = raw
```

and expose `client.classify_error(e)` for SDKs where we can't catch at call site.

sam: From infra: we can tighten the header behavior for the next deploy — ensure `Retry-After` is seconds and include `x-redwood-error-code` header for machine-readability. Will coordinate.

elaine: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) update docs sample apps to use typed errors + the helper, 2) add a small conformance test in SDK CI that error mapping matches the table in devex docs.

raj: I can open a PR for python + typescript SDKs with the error classes and helpers. Will add unit tests and a snippet for the docs.

dev-bot: Scheduled: SDK error-contraction sync tomorrow 09:30 PT — raj assigned.

sam: Quick question — do we want the SDKs to auto-retry by default for 429/503 or leave that as opt-in? My vote: opt-in with `auto_retry=True` explicit flag and sensible defaults (exponential backoff, respect `retry_after`).

elaine: Opt-in is safer for adoption. For hosted quickstart we can showcase `auto_retry=True` so newcomers see the pattern. Also add a note in console UX around which responses are retriable.

raj: Sounds good. I'll include param in client constructor and a short example in sample-apps repo.

elaine: Thanks — priorities: 1) add error_code header (sam), 2) SDK typed exceptions + classify helper (raj), 3) update sample apps and docs (me + docs). Let's sync after the PRs. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll post a deploy ETA in infra channel when the header change is ready.

raj: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/482 (draft). Comments welcome.

elaine: Reviewing now. Quick note — include migration notes: how to map old generic catches to new typed handlers. Many users rely on `except Exception:` patterns.

raj: Will add a small section and a code example.

sam: If anyone needs a reproducible test event for 429 I can generate token-muzzled requests in staging.

elaine: Perfect, that will help the SDK tests. Thanks all.
